Second starter, started 10 Feb 2025. Wanted a levain with no acid tang for the croissants and the brioche buns. Yeast water is fruit plus water plus sugar, the wild yeast on the fruit skins does the work.

## Setup

- 750 ml clip-top jar, sterilised with boiling water
- 120 g Lexia raisins, unsulphured (sulphured ones don't ferment, learned that on the first go, 2 Feb, nothing happened in 6 days)
- peel of 1 Braeburn apple
- 400 ml filtered water at 28°C
- 1 tsp honey
- on top of the fridge-freezer, about 26°C

Shake twice a day, open the lid once a day to let gas out.

## Timeline

- day 1-2: nothing, raisins at the bottom
- day 3: raisins plumped up and floating, tiny bubbles
- day 4: fizz when shaken, smells faintly of wine
- day 5: hisses when opened like a can of cider, foam on top. Ready.

So 5 days from 10 Feb, ready on the 15th. Strain the liquid, that's the yeast water.

## Building a levain

1. 100 g yeast water + 100 g strong white, 26°C, 8 hours, doubled
2. second build: all of that + 100 g flour + 50 g water, 6 hours
3. then it behaves like a mild 1:1:1 levain

First build is slow, after that it speeds up. Not as strong as Gary (the sourdough, see [[Sourdough starter]]), it needs about 30% longer bulk.

## Results

Croissant test on 22 Feb with 15% yeast-water levain replacing half the commercial yeast: softer crumb, sweeter, slightly more open honeycomb. Notes in [[Laminated croissant dough]]. Tash preferred them blind, 4 out of 5 people at the truck did too.

## Keeping it going

- fridge at 4°C between uses
- refresh every 10 days: pour off half, top up with water, add 40 g fresh raisins
- if it smells like vinegar it's gone acetic, start again. Same failure mode as an over-brewed [[Kombucha SCOBY]] batch.
